lessons.title: Vocabulary and Grammar Review
lessons.notes_html:
Kinds of Sentences

  • Declarative: The mason is building the wall. / The lion has killed the deer. / The tailor will alter my shirt tomorrow.
  • Exclamatory: What a pity we have lost the match! / What a beautiful sight! / How beautiful is the baby!
  • Interrogative: Did he break the window? / Was the doctor serving patients?
  • Imperative: Finish your work at once. / Do not beat the poor boy.

Homophones — Choose the Right Word

  • You look rather pale. He went down the hill to fetch a pail of water.
  • I have read through all your answers. The boy threw the ball out of the window.
  • On the whole you have done very well. There is a hole in my shoe.
  • The headmaster will not accept your explanation. I have seen all important cities except Quetta.
  • Can you see the picture over there? They have all done their work very well.
  • Mother gave me a piece of cake. We should live in peace with each other.

Homographs in Sentences

  • left — (a) He left his bag at home. (b) Turn to the left side.
  • bat — (a) A bat hangs upside down in the cave. (b) He bought a new cricket bat.
  • ring — (a) She wears a gold ring. (b) Ring the bell at once.
  • bow — (a) The boys bow before the teacher respectfully. (b) He shoots arrows with a bow.
  • letter — (a) I wrote a letter to my friend. (b) 'B' is a letter of the English alphabet.

Joining with Conjunctions

  • The piper played and the children danced.
  • The letter was neither from me nor from my sister.
  • Jamal works hard but his brother is lazy.
  • I went to the shop and bought some vegetables.
  • You must start at once or you will be late.
  • He must be tired because he has been working since morning.
  • I am thinking to visit Islamabad for my vacation and also stay there for the party.

Indirect Speech

  • Alia said that she worked in a school.
  • They said that they were playing hockey.
  • Ali said that his father had worked in fields.
  • Hadi said that he had not seen Naveed that day.
  • She said that she was walking down the hill.

mcqs.q: 'What a beautiful sight!' is a/an ______ sentence.
mcqs.why: It expresses strong feeling, like 'What a pity we have lost the match!' and 'How beautiful is the baby!' — exclamatory sentences.

mcqs.q: 'Finish your work at once' is a/an ______ sentence.
mcqs.why: It gives an order — an imperative sentence, like 'Do not beat the poor boy.'

mcqs.q: You look rather ______. Aren't you feeling well?
mcqs.why: Pale means light-coloured (of the face); a pail is a bucket — 'He went to fetch a pail of water.'

mcqs.q: The headmaster will not ______ your explanation.
mcqs.why: Accept means to take or agree to; except means leaving out — 'all important cities except Quetta.'

mcqs.q: Mother gave me a ______ of cake.
mcqs.why: A piece is a part of something; peace is calm — 'We should live in peace with each other.'

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses 'ring' as a homograph correctly for BOTH meanings?
options: The ring is round; the ring is gold
She wears a gold ring; ring the bell at once
Ring the bell; the bell rings
A ring of people stood there
mcqs.why: Ring is a homograph: a gold ring (jewellery) and ring the bell (an action) — same spelling, different meanings.

mcqs.q: 'The letter was ______ from me ______ from my sister.'
mcqs.why: The solved joining uses the correlative pair neither–nor for two negatives.

mcqs.q: 'You must start at once ______ you will be late.'
mcqs.why: 'Or' joins the warning: start at once or you will be late. 'Because' would give a reason, which does not fit here.

mcqs.q: Hadi said, 'I have not seen Naveed today.' → indirect: ______.
options: Hadi said that he had not seen Naveed that day
Hadi said that he has not seen Naveed today
Hadi said that I have not seen Naveed today
Hadi said that he had not seen Naveed today
mcqs.why: Present perfect becomes past perfect (have not seen → had not seen) and 'today' becomes 'that day' in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: 'I have read ______ all your answers.'
mcqs.why: Through means from one side to the other / completely; threw is the past of throw — 'The boy threw the ball out of the window.'

lessons.title: Writing: Dialogue on a Cricket Match and Essay on Cleanliness
lessons.notes_html:
Dialogue on a Cricket Match (Model)

Usman: Assalam-o-Alaikum, Bilal! Did you see last night's match? Bilal: Wa-Alaikum-us-Salam! Yes, I saw the whole match. Pakistan played wonderfully. Usman: The batting was superb, but the last over was breathtaking. Bilal: True! We needed ten runs from six balls. Usman: And our batsman hit a six and a four — the crowd went mad with joy. Bilal: The fielding was also excellent. Two run-outs changed the game. Usman: That is why I love cricket; it teaches teamwork and sportsmanship. Bilal: Let us also practise daily and play a friendly match on Sunday. Usman: Agreed! See you at the ground.

Essay — 'Keeping Our Surroundings Clean' (Model)

Mind map: Centre — Keeping Our Surroundings Clean. Branches: (1) Why clean — health, beauty, Allah loves cleanliness. (2) At home — dustbins, no littering. (3) At school — clean classrooms and grounds. (4) In streets — do not throw garbage, plant trees. (5) Results — fewer diseases, fresh air, beautiful Earth.

Essay: 'Cleanliness is half of faith, and keeping our surroundings clean is our duty. A dirty environment spreads diseases and makes life unpleasant, while clean surroundings keep us healthy and happy. We should throw litter only in dustbins, keep our homes, classrooms and streets clean, and plant more trees. We must not spit or throw garbage in public places, and we should stop others from doing so politely. If every citizen keeps his own surroundings clean, our whole country will become clean and beautiful, and the Earth will remain a beautiful place to live in.'

mcqs.q: In the model dialogue, how many runs were needed from the last six balls?
mcqs.why: Bilal says: 'We needed ten runs from six balls' — and the batsman hit a six and a four.

mcqs.q: What changed the game in the dialogue?
mcqs.why: Bilal says: 'The fielding was also excellent. Two run-outs changed the game.'

mcqs.q: Usman loves cricket because it teaches ______.
mcqs.why: Usman says: 'That is why I love cricket; it teaches teamwork and sportsmanship.'

mcqs.q: The two friends decide to ______.
options: join a club in another city
practise daily and play a friendly match on Sunday
mcqs.why: Bilal suggests practising daily and playing a friendly match on Sunday; Usman agrees: 'See you at the ground.'

mcqs.q: The essay begins with the saying ______.
mcqs.why: The model essay opens: 'Cleanliness is half of faith, and keeping our surroundings clean is our duty.'

mcqs.q: According to the essay, a dirty environment ______.
options: spreads diseases and makes life unpleasant
mcqs.why: A dirty environment spreads diseases and makes life unpleasant, while clean surroundings keep us healthy and happy.

mcqs.q: We should throw litter ______.
mcqs.why: The essay instructs: throw litter only in dustbins; keep homes, classrooms and streets clean; plant more trees.

mcqs.q: In the essay's mind map, the results of cleanliness are ______.
options: fewer diseases, fresh air and a beautiful Earth
mcqs.why: Mind-map branch (5) Results: fewer diseases, fresh air, beautiful Earth.

mcqs.q: The mind map's 'at school' branch asks for ______.
mcqs.why: Branch (3) At school — clean classrooms and grounds; branch (2) At home — dustbins, no littering; branch (4) In streets — do not throw garbage, plant trees.

mcqs.q: The essay ends with the idea that if every citizen keeps his own surroundings clean, ______.
options: the whole country will become clean and beautiful
diseases will vanish in a day
mcqs.why: The conclusion: 'If every citizen keeps his own surroundings clean, our whole country will become clean and beautiful.'

lessons.title: Reading: Mountaineering
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Mountaineering?

Mountain climbing is called mountaineering. It is a classified and well-organised sport, taught as an independent subject in regular institutions all over the world. Mount Everest is the highest peak of the world; it was conquered for the first time in 1953 by Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary. The entire world admired this great task, and since then climbers have always tried to climb Mount Everest.

A Risky Sport

Yes, mountaineering is a risky and dangerous sport — one of the most dangerous and challenging sports. It involves the highest risk: climbers cross narrow ledges and steep hillsides in bad weather; the oxygen becomes less as they climb; storms may sweep away their tents; and there have been instances of the loss of valuable lives, such as Muhammad Ali Sadpara, one of Pakistan's most celebrated climbers, who lost his life with two fellow climbers in an attempt at climbing K2 in the winter of 2021.

Problems a Mountaineer Faces

  • Less oxygen at height, making breathing difficult, so artificial oxygen must be used continuously.
  • Unpredictable weather and unexpected storms whose strong winds may sweep away his tent.
  • Snowfall while climbing, and walking through soft snow.
  • The danger of frostbite, in which a part of the body may become completely numb or damaged due to stoppage of blood circulation.
  • He risks his life itself, knowing he might never return.

Qualities of a Mountaineer

A mountaineer must have the spirit of adventure, which encourages him to continue his struggle till he conquers the peak. He must be prepared to accept the challenge of risks and hardships, and needs extraordinary courage in bad weather and dangerous situations. Besides physical strength, he should have spiritual powers of mind and heart, which provide him with strong willpower and heroic courage. He attempts the peak fearlessly, keeping his eye on his goal without being daunted by problems.

Word Meanings

  • fascinated — extremely interested. extraordinary — very unusual, special.
  • risk — the possibility of something bad happening. conquer — to gain by overcoming obstacles or opposition.
  • struggle — to experience difficulty to do something. ledges — narrow, flat areas like shelves sticking out from a cliff.
  • valuable — important, useful or beneficial. circumstances — events or conditions connected with what is happening.
  • artificial — man-made, not natural. unpredictable — that cannot be foretold; changing suddenly.
  • frostbite — injury of body parts by severe cold, stopping blood circulation. willpower — strong determination of mind and heart. fearlessly — without fear; bravely.

mcqs.q: Mountain climbing is called ______.
mcqs.why: The text states: mountain climbing is called mountaineering, a classified and well-organised sport taught as an independent subject in institutions.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of the world?
mcqs.why: Mount Everest is the highest peak of the world, conquered for the first time in 1953.

mcqs.q: Mount Everest was conquered for the first time in 1953 by ______.
options: Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary
Muhammad Ali Sadpara and his team
mcqs.why: The entire world admired the great task of Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary in 1953.

mcqs.q: Muhammad Ali Sadpara lost his life ______.
options: in an attempt at climbing K2 in the winter of 2021, with two fellow climbers
mcqs.why: The text gives Sadpara's loss — with two fellow climbers on K2 in winter 2021 — as an instance of the loss of valuable lives in this risky sport.

mcqs.q: Why does a mountaineer use artificial oxygen?
options: Because the oxygen becomes less at height and breathing becomes difficult
mcqs.why: In those circumstances the supply of artificial oxygen is essential, and the mountaineer uses it continuously.

mcqs.q: Frostbite is ______.
options: injury of body parts by severe cold, stopping blood circulation
mcqs.why: An unprotected climber may get frostbite and a part of his body may become numb, due to stoppage of blood circulation.

mcqs.q: 'Ledges' are ______.
options: narrow, flat areas like shelves sticking out from a cliff
mcqs.why: The meanings exercise defines ledges as narrow, flat areas like shelves sticking out from a cliff, which the climber must cross.

mcqs.q: Which quality helps a mountaineer continue his struggle till he conquers the peak?
mcqs.why: The spirit of adventure encourages the mountaineer to continue his struggle, along with extraordinary courage, willpower and fearlessness.

mcqs.q: Besides physical strength, a mountaineer needs ______.
options: spiritual powers of mind and heart, giving strong willpower and heroic courage
mcqs.why: The text says he should have spiritual powers of mind and heart, which provide him with strong willpower and heroic courage to achieve his goal.

mcqs.q: 'Unpredictable' weather is weather that ______.
options: cannot be foretold and changes suddenly
mcqs.why: As climbers go higher, the weather becomes unpredictable — it cannot be foretold and changes suddenly, bringing unexpected storms.

lessons.title: Vocabulary: Tongue Twisters, Synonyms and Antonyms, Noun Phrase and Noun Clause
lessons.notes_html:
Tongue Twisters — Alliteration and Assonance

Alliteration: repetition of the same initial consonant sound in nearby words. Assonance: repetition of the same vowel sound in nearby words.

  • 'Good, better, best, / Never let it rest, / Till your good is better, / And your better best.' — Alliteration: the 'b' sound in better/best. Assonance: the short 'e' sound in better, best, rest.
  • 'Fanny Fetter found a fan...' — Alliteration: the 'f' sound in Fanny, Fetter, found, fan, felt. Assonance: the short 'a/e' sounds in Fanny, fan, Fetter, better.
  • 'How many cans can a canner can...' — Alliteration: the 'c/k' sound in cans, can, canner. Assonance: the short 'a' sound in can, cans, canner.
  • Own tongue twister (model): 'Ali the able athlete ate eight apples at an amazing pace.' — alliteration (the 'a' sound repeated).

Synonyms and Antonyms

  • fascinated: syn extremely interested, captivated; ant bored, uninterested.
  • extraordinary: syn very unusual, remarkable; ant ordinary, common.
  • risk: syn danger, hazard; ant safety, security.
  • conquer: syn overcome, defeat; ant surrender, lose.
  • struggle: syn strive, labour; ant rest, give up.
  • valuable: syn precious, useful; ant worthless, useless.
  • artificial: syn man-made, unnatural; ant natural, real.
  • unpredictable: syn uncertain, changeable; ant predictable, certain.
  • fearlessly: syn bravely, boldly; ant fearfully, timidly.
  • dangerous: syn risky, hazardous; ant safe, secure.

Noun Phrase and Noun Clause

A noun phrase is a phrase that acts like a noun in the sentence. A noun clause is a group of words which contains a subject and predicate of its own and does the work of a noun — as object, subject or complement.

  • 'when he will come' — Noun Clause (object of 'knows'). 'the time of his coming' — Noun Phrase.
  • 'that he had succeeded' — Noun Clause. 'his success' — Noun Phrase.
  • 'why he succeeded' — Noun Clause. 'the reason of his success' — Noun Phrase.

mcqs.q: Alliteration is ______.
options: the repetition of the same vowel sound in nearby words
the repetition of the same initial consonant sound in nearby words
mcqs.why: Alliteration repeats initial consonant sounds — the 'f' in 'Fanny Fetter found a fan'; assonance repeats vowel sounds.

mcqs.q: In 'Good, better, best', the alliteration is the ______ sound.
mcqs.why: The exercise points out the 'b' sound in better/best as alliteration, and the short 'e' in better, best, rest as assonance.

mcqs.q: Assonance in 'How many cans can a canner can' is ______.
options: the short 'a' sound in can, cans, canner
mcqs.why: The short 'a' vowel sound repeats — assonance; the 'c/k' sound repetition is the alliteration in the same twister.

mcqs.q: What is the antonym of 'conquer'?
mcqs.why: Conquer — synonym overcome, defeat; antonym surrender, lose, as listed in the synonyms and antonyms exercise.

mcqs.q: What is the synonym of 'artificial'?
mcqs.why: Artificial means man-made, unnatural; its antonyms are natural and real.

mcqs.q: 'when he will come' in 'No one knows when he will come' is a ______.
mcqs.why: It has its own subject and predicate and works as the object of 'knows' — a noun clause; 'the time of his coming' is only a noun phrase.

mcqs.q: 'the reason of his success' is a ______.
mcqs.why: It acts like a noun but has no subject–predicate pair of its own, so it is a noun phrase; 'why he succeeded' is the noun clause.

mcqs.q: A noun clause does the work of a noun as ______.
mcqs.why: The book defines a noun clause as a group of words with its own subject and predicate doing the work of a noun — as object, subject or complement.

mcqs.q: What is the antonym of 'fearlessly'?
mcqs.why: Fearlessly — synonym bravely, boldly; antonym fearfully, timidly.

mcqs.q: Which tongue twister shows alliteration with the 'a' sound?
options: 'How many cans can a canner can'
'Ali the able athlete ate eight apples at an amazing pace'
mcqs.why: The model tongue twister repeats the initial 'a' sound: Ali, able, athlete, ate, eight, apples, amazing — alliteration.

lessons.title: Grammar and Writing: Reported Speech, Proofreading, Sensory Language and Descriptive Essay
lessons.notes_html:
Direct and Indirect Speech — Past Tenses

Rules from the book: simple past changes into past perfect; past continuous changes into past perfect continuous; past perfect remains past perfect.

  • My brother told me that he had not gone out at the weekend.
  • Amina said that her friends and she had gone to the museum the day before.
  • Hamid told me that he had been waiting for the bus when I arrived.
  • I told her that Noor had not gone there.
  • Fatima said that she had been going home.
  • You told me that I had changed my mind.

Proofreading — Corrected Passage

'Once, the most challenging assignment was to conquer the highest peak of the world, Mount Everest. This dream came into reality by Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary in 1953. The entire world admired this great task. It has been a regular feature for the climbers of the world since then, and many people have also tried to climb Mount Everest.' (Corrections: capitalisation of Once and Mount Everest; spellings — assignment, peak, admired, feature, since; punctuation added.)

Sensory Language

Sensory language = words that connect to the five senses: see, hear, smell, touch, taste. (A few words, such as dusty and dry, can appeal to more than one sense.)

  • Sight: dim, dark, fiery, crooked, crowded, deserted, beautiful, dusty.
  • Hearing: rumble, loud, roar, screech, scratching.
  • Smell: smoky, stinky, dusty.
  • Taste: salty, stale, dry, raw.
  • Touch: moist, sweaty, bumpy, rough, sharp, dry, raw, scratching.

Descriptive Essay — 'Dangerous Sports' (Model)

Mind map: Topic Idea — Dangerous sports and their thrill. Introduction — some sports attract people because of danger. Paragraph 1 — Mountaineering: steep hillsides, narrow ledges, storms, frostbite. Paragraph 2 — Other dangerous sports: car racing, boxing, skydiving. Paragraph 3 — Why people love them: spirit of adventure, courage, willpower. Paragraph 4 — Safety: training, tools and kits, institutions. Conclusion — dangerous sports strengthen bravery if practised with training and care.

Essay extract: 'The climber walks through soft snow on narrow ledges; the cold wind roars around him, his hands feel numb, and the sharp ice shines in the dim light. A sudden storm may sweep away his tent, and frostbite may damage his body. Car racing fills the air with the screech of tyres and the smell of burning fuel... Dangerous sports are now taught in regular institutions with advanced tools and kits to ensure safety. In short, dangerous sports strengthen the qualities of bravery and courage, but they must be practised with proper training, protection and strong willpower.'

mcqs.q: In indirect speech, the simple past changes into ______.
mcqs.why: The book's rules for this set: simple past → past perfect; past continuous → past perfect continuous; past perfect remains past perfect.

mcqs.q: Amina said, 'My friends and I went to the museum yesterday.' → indirect: ______.
options: Amina said that her friends and she went to the museum yesterday
Amina said that her friends and she had gone to the museum the day before
Amina said that my friends and I had gone to the museum yesterday
Amina said that her friends and she go to the museum the day before
mcqs.why: 'Went' (simple past) becomes 'had gone' (past perfect), and 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'.

mcqs.q: Hamid said, 'I was waiting for the bus when you arrived.' → indirect: ______.
options: Hamid told me that he was waiting for the bus when I arrived
Hamid told me that I had been waiting for the bus
Hamid told me that he had been waiting for the bus when I arrived
Hamid told me that he had waited for the bus yesterday
mcqs.why: Past continuous (was waiting) changes into past perfect continuous (had been waiting) in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: In the proofread passage, the corrected sentence begins ______.
options: 'Once, the most challenging assignment was to conquer the highest peak of the world, Mount Everest'
mcqs.why: Proofreading corrected capitalisation (Once, Mount Everest), spellings (assignment, peak, admired, feature, since) and punctuation.

mcqs.q: Sensory language is language that ______.
options: connects to the five senses: see, hear, smell, touch, taste
rhymes at the end of lines
mcqs.why: Sensory words appeal to sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch — the basis of descriptive writing in this unit.

mcqs.q: Which word belongs to the sense of HEARING?
mcqs.why: Hearing words: rumble, loud, roar, screech, scratching. Salty is taste, bumpy is touch, dim is sight.

mcqs.q: Which word belongs to the sense of TASTE?
mcqs.why: Taste words: salty, stale, dry, raw. Roar is hearing, smoky is smell, rough is touch.

mcqs.q: In the descriptive essay, car racing fills the air with ______.
options: the roar of the crowd only
the screech of tyres and the smell of burning fuel
mcqs.why: The essay uses sensory language for racing: 'the screech of tyres and the smell of burning fuel' — hearing and smell together.

mcqs.q: The essay's conclusion is that dangerous sports ______.
options: strengthen bravery and courage, but must be practised with proper training, protection and strong willpower
mcqs.why: Conclusion: dangerous sports strengthen the qualities of bravery and courage, but they must be practised with proper training, protection and strong willpower.

mcqs.q: Which dangerous sports are named in the essay's mind map besides mountaineering?
mcqs.why: Paragraph 2 of the mind map covers other dangerous sports: car racing, boxing, skydiving — speed, noise, risk.

lessons.title: Talk Time and Reading: Dignity of Labour
lessons.notes_html:
Appreciating Our Helpers

We can appreciate the people who help us daily — garbage picker, maids, drivers, watchman — by treating them with respect and dignity, because no job is inferior. We should speak to them politely, use courtesy words like 'please' and 'thank you', pay them their wages on time, not overload them with work, and help them in their need or illness. We should never shout at or look down upon them, for they make our work easier every day. (In the Talk Time dialogue, Saad himself did the kitchen work instead of disturbing his unwell mother, and taught his little sister Taniya to make a vegetable sandwich — ingredients: cheese, bread, cucumber, carrot, cabbage, ketchup.)

Meaning of the Title

The dignity of labour means respect and value given to all forms of work; it refers to equal respect for the jobs that involve manual labour. There is no job or profession which is inferior, and we must respect professionals of all fields.

Farmers — The Backbone of Society

Farmers are the backbone of society because they cultivate the crops, and we get the food that we eat every day. The entire population depends upon farmers; if farmers stop cultivating crops, there will be famine and starvation. Ahmad's father is a farmer who farms wheat, barley and rice; he works from morning to evening in the fields, so he comes home exhausted. He has received education of agriculture from Faisalabad Agriculture University; because of his knowledge of cultivation and the right fertilisers, he has bumper crops every year and earns good profit — unlike many uneducated farmers who face loss.

The 'Golden Sparrow'

Before the creation of Pakistan, the subcontinent was called 'Golden Sparrow' because of the fertility of the land and bumper crops; that is why many nations tried to occupy this land.

How a Country May Progress in Agriculture

By educating its farmers and facilitating them in their needs, by painstaking research in this field, and by giving farmers the fruit of their labour and due respect in society, so that the number of farmers may increase. The government should encourage farmers by introducing more productive projects in the field of agriculture.

Word Meanings

  • backbone — the chief support of a system. cultivating — growing (crops).
  • famine — lack of food and grains. starvation — severe hunger.
  • exhausted — weary, tired. bumper — large, fine or successful (crop).
  • progress — development; moving forward. fertility — ability (of land) to grow crops.
  • agricultural — relating to farming. betterment — improvement.
  • appreciated — valued and respected. (Note: the book's glossary prints a wrong meaning against 'appreciated'; the correct meaning is valued and respected.)

mcqs.q: The 'dignity of labour' means ______.
options: respect and value given to all forms of work, with no job inferior
mcqs.why: The dignity of labour means equal respect for all work, including manual labour; there is no job or profession which is inferior.

mcqs.q: Farmers are called the backbone of society because ______.
options: they cultivate the crops and provide the food we eat every day
mcqs.why: The entire population depends upon farmers; if they stop cultivating crops, there will be famine and starvation.

mcqs.q: Ahmad's father comes home exhausted because ______.
options: he travels to the city daily
he works from morning to evening in the fields
he drives a tractor for others
mcqs.why: He is a farmer of wheat, barley and rice who works from morning to evening in the fields, so he comes home exhausted (weary, tired).

mcqs.q: Why does Ahmad's father have bumper crops every year?
options: He has the largest fields in the village
He has agriculture education from Faisalabad Agriculture University and knows cultivation and the right fertilisers
His land is near a river only
mcqs.why: Because of his education and knowledge of crops and fertilisers he earns good profit, unlike many uneducated farmers who face loss.

mcqs.q: The subcontinent was called 'Golden Sparrow' because of ______.
options: the fertility of the land and bumper crops
mcqs.why: Before the creation of Pakistan, the subcontinent was called 'Golden Sparrow' for its fertile land and bumper crops, which attracted many nations to occupy it.

mcqs.q: A country may progress in agriculture by ______.
options: educating and facilitating farmers, doing research, and giving farmers due respect
mcqs.why: Progress comes from educating farmers, facilitating their needs, painstaking research, productive government projects, and giving farmers the fruit of their labour and due respect.

mcqs.q: How should we treat our daily helpers?
options: With respect and dignity — politely, with courtesy words, wages on time and no overloading
By paying them whenever we like
mcqs.why: We should never shout at or look down upon the garbage picker, maid, driver or watchman; gratitude encourages them and teaches the dignity of labour.

mcqs.q: In the Talk Time dialogue, Saad made a vegetable sandwich for ______.
options: his little sister Taniya, while their mother rested
mcqs.why: Saad did the kitchen work himself instead of disturbing his unwell mother and taught Taniya to make the sandwich (cheese, bread, cucumber, carrot, cabbage, ketchup).

mcqs.q: 'Bumper' (crop) means ______.
mcqs.why: The glossary defines a bumper crop as large, fine or successful — Ahmad's father has bumper crops every year and earns good profit.

mcqs.q: The book's glossary prints a wrong meaning against 'appreciated'. 'Appreciated' correctly means ______.
mcqs.why: The solved content itself corrects the book's glossary misprint: appreciated means valued and respected — if farmers are respected and appreciated, the country will progress.

lessons.title: Vocabulary and Grammar: Antonyms, Linking and Helping Verbs, Reported Speech
lessons.notes_html:
Antonyms

  • dignity — disgrace/dishonour; urban — rural; stop — start/continue; live — die.
  • respected — disrespected/dishonoured; increase — decrease; productive — unproductive; tired — fresh/energetic.

Linking, Action and Helping Verbs

Action verbs express action or state. Linking verbs link the subject to a predicate (a description). Helping verbs work together with the main verb and change its mood or tense.

  • Action verbs: Hamid went to his room. Alia is working in the hospital ('is' is helping here). He goes to school. She will speak the truth ('will' helping). They are cooking food. The policeman is doing his duty well.
  • Linking verb: Pollution from vehicles is dangerous for health. ('is' links 'pollution' with 'dangerous'.)
  • More linking verbs: I am not well today. Pollution has become a major problem ('become' linking, 'has' helping). He was indecisive. You look tired. That sounds a good idea. Ahmad is an honest boy. The baskets were full of apples. It was hot yesterday. The jigsaw puzzle proved too difficult.
  • Helping verb: She will visit her aunt tomorrow ('will' helps the action verb 'visit').

Direct and Indirect Speech — Future

In indirect speech, 'will' changes into 'would' and 'shall' into 'should'.

  • I said that we would wait for him/her an hour only.
  • She said that she would never do such things.
  • They told me that they would marry the next year.
  • She said that she would cook dinner for the guests.
  • He said that I should study that book.

mcqs.q: What is the antonym of 'productive'?
mcqs.why: The antonyms exercise pairs productive — unproductive, along with dignity — disgrace, urban — rural, increase — decrease, tired — fresh/energetic.

mcqs.q: What is the antonym of 'urban'?
mcqs.why: Urban (city) is opposite to rural (village/countryside) in the antonyms list of this unit.

mcqs.q: In 'Pollution from vehicles is dangerous for health', 'is' is a ______ verb.
mcqs.why: 'Is' links the subject 'pollution' with its description 'dangerous' — a linking verb; but in 'Alia is working', 'is' is a helping verb.

mcqs.q: In 'She will visit her aunt tomorrow', 'will' is a ______ verb.
mcqs.why: Helping verbs work with the main verb and change its mood or tense: 'will' helps the action verb 'visit'. The sentence has no linking verb.

mcqs.q: In 'You look tired after attending the wedding', 'look' is a ______ verb.
mcqs.why: 'Look' links 'you' with the description 'tired' — a linking verb, like am, was, sounds, is, were and proved in the exercise.

mcqs.q: In 'Pollution from buses has become a major problem', ______ is the linking verb and ______ is the helping verb.
mcqs.why: The solved answer explains: 'become' is the linking verb and 'has' is the helping verb in 'has become'.

mcqs.q: Action verbs express ______.
mcqs.why: The book defines: action verbs express action or state; linking verbs link the subject to a predicate; helping verbs work with the main verb.

mcqs.q: She said, 'I will cook dinner for the guests.' → indirect: ______.
options: She said that she will cook dinner for the guests
She said that she would cook dinner for the guests
She said that I would cook dinner for the guests
She said that she should cook dinner tomorrow
mcqs.why: In indirect speech 'will' changes into 'would': She said that she would cook dinner for the guests.

mcqs.q: He said, 'You shall study this book.' → indirect: ______.
options: He said that I shall study this book
He said that you shall study that book
He said that I should study that book
He said that I would study this book
mcqs.why: 'Shall' changes into 'should' in indirect speech, and 'this' becomes 'that': He said that I should study that book.

mcqs.q: They told me, 'We will marry next year.' → indirect: ______.
options: They told me that we will marry next year
They told me that they would marry next year today
They told me that they shall marry the next year
They told me that they would marry the next year
mcqs.why: 'Will' becomes 'would' and 'next year' becomes 'the next year' in indirect speech.

lessons.title: Writing: Recipe, Essay on Migration and Letter to a Sibling
lessons.notes_html:
Recipe — Fruit Chaat (Model)

Ingredients: 1. Two apples. 2. Two bananas. 3. One cup of grapes. 4. Two oranges. 5. Chaat masala and a little sugar. Procedure: 1. Wash all the fruits well. 2. Peel the bananas and oranges. 3. Cut the apples, bananas and oranges into small pieces. 4. Put all the pieces and grapes in a big bowl. 5. Sprinkle chaat masala and sugar on them, mix gently, and serve fresh.

Essay — Rural to Urban Migration (Model)

Graphic organiser: Reasons — (1) tough living style of village life; (2) farming thought to be a low-paid profession; (3) lack of education, hospitals and jobs in villages. Effects — (1) the number of farmers is decreasing day by day; (2) cities become overcrowded; (3) agricultural production falls. Solutions — educate and facilitate farmers; give them due respect; start productive projects in villages.

Essay extract: 'Many people have migrated to urban areas because of the tough living style of village life... Villages also lack good schools, hospitals and other jobs. As a result, cities become overcrowded, slums grow, and the country loses the farmers who are the backbone of society; if farmers stop cultivating, there will be famine and starvation. To stop this migration, the government should facilitate the villagers: build schools and hospitals in villages, educate the farmers about modern methods and fertilisers, and introduce productive projects in the field of agriculture.'

Letter to a Younger Sibling (Model)

Format (from the book): Address, Date, Greetings, Body, Closing farewell, Signature. Model: '48 Garden Block, Lahore. August 12, 2022. Dear Ahmed, ... I am writing this letter because mother has told me that you often speak rudely to our maid and driver at home. Dear brother, this is very wrong. The helpers work hard for us the whole day; they make our work easier and deserve our respect, for there is dignity in every labour. Please have a good attitude with them... Always use courtesy words with them — say "please", "thank you" and "sorry" — and never shout at them... Your loving brother, Aslam.'

mcqs.q: A recipe is organised into ______.
mcqs.why: The model recipe (Fruit Chaat) lists the ingredients first and then the procedure step by step — the standard recipe format.

mcqs.q: In the Fruit Chaat recipe, what is sprinkled on the fruit at the end?
options: Chaat masala and a little sugar
mcqs.why: Step 5: 'Sprinkle chaat masala and sugar on them, mix gently, and serve fresh.'

mcqs.q: Which fruit in the recipe is NOT peeled?
options: Apples (and grapes) — only bananas and oranges are peeled
mcqs.why: Step 2 says peel the bananas and oranges; the apples are only washed and cut, and the grapes go in whole.

mcqs.q: Which is a REASON for rural to urban migration in the essay?
options: Lack of education, hospitals and jobs in villages
mcqs.why: Reasons: tough village living style, farming thought to be low-paid, and lack of education, hospitals and jobs in villages.

mcqs.q: Which is an EFFECT of migration in the essay?
options: Cities become overcrowded and the number of farmers decreases
mcqs.why: Effects: farmers decrease day by day, cities become overcrowded, slums grow, and agricultural production falls.

mcqs.q: To stop migration, the government should ______.
options: force people to stay in villages
build schools and hospitals in villages and educate farmers about modern methods and fertilisers
mcqs.why: Solutions: facilitate villagers with schools and hospitals, educate farmers, introduce productive projects, and give farmers the fruit of their labour and due respect.

mcqs.q: The format of the model letter is ______.
options: Address, Date, Greetings, Body, Closing farewell, Signature
mcqs.why: The book's letter format is: Address, Date, Greetings, Body, Closing farewell, Signature — as in the model letter from Aslam to Ahmed.

mcqs.q: Why does Aslam write the letter to Ahmed?
options: To reprimand him for speaking rudely to the maid and driver at home
To invite him to a party
To tell him about his exams
mcqs.why: Mother told Aslam that Ahmed often speaks rudely to the helpers; the letter advises him to have a good attitude with them.

mcqs.q: Which courtesy words does the letter advise Ahmed to use?
mcqs.why: The letter says: Always use courtesy words with them — say 'please', 'thank you' and 'sorry' — and never shout at them.

mcqs.q: The letter says the helpers deserve our respect because ______.
options: there is dignity in every labour and they make our work easier
mcqs.why: The helpers work hard the whole day and make our work easier; they deserve respect, for there is dignity in every labour.

lessons.title: Reading: Give to Your Country (Poem)
lessons.notes_html:
Laws Keep Us Happy and Well

All the laws that are made in our country are laws to keep us happy and well, peaceful and unafraid. Because the laws protect our lives, property and rights, we live in peace without fear, and so remain happy and well. 'Peaceful and unafraid' means living in peace, free from disturbance, and feeling no fear or anxiety.

Our Debt to the Country

We owe a debt to our country because our country is great and good to us: it gives us protection, peace and laws that keep us happy and well. We can pay back this debt with patriotic words and deeds — by giving the country our service, giving her our all and our best, and letting our actions and words prove a wealth of love for her.

The Needs of the Country

The needs of the country are the service, loyalty and hard work of its citizens: honest work in every field, respect for laws, unity, and sacrifice for the nation's progress and defence. We can fulfil them by answering the country's needs under the name of citizenship — giving her service and our best, and paying our debt with patriotic words and deeds.

How I Want to Serve (Model)

'I want to serve my country by becoming a good, educated and honest citizen. I will study hard, obey the laws, keep my surroundings clean, help the poor, and, when I grow up, serve Pakistan as a teacher so that every child of my country can read and write.'

Word Meanings

  • peaceful — free from disturbance, tranquil. unafraid — feeling no fear or anxiety.
  • deserve — to be worthy of something because of what one has done. (Note: the book glossary prints 'do something/show some quality' against 'deserve'; the correct sense in the poem is 'to be worthy of'.)
  • citizenship — the position of being a citizen of a country. patriotic — expressing devotion for one's country.

mcqs.q: How do the laws of our country keep us happy and well?
options: They protect our lives, property and rights, so we live in peace without fear
They let us do anything we like
mcqs.why: All the laws are made to keep us happy and well, peaceful and unafraid, because they protect our lives, property and rights.

mcqs.q: 'Peaceful and unafraid' means ______.
options: living in peace, free from disturbance, and feeling no fear or anxiety
mcqs.why: The poem's phrase means a calm life without fear of harm or injustice, protected by the laws of the country.

mcqs.q: Why do we owe a debt to our country?
options: Because the country lends us money
Because the country is great and good to us, giving protection, peace and laws
mcqs.why: We owe the debt for the country's goodness — protection, peace and laws that keep us happy and well.

mcqs.q: How can we pay back our debt to the country?
options: By paying a special tax only
By praising it in songs only
With patriotic words and deeds — giving her our service, our all and our best
mcqs.why: The debt is paid with patriotic words and deeds: service, our all and our best, and actions and words proving a wealth of love for her.

mcqs.q: What are the needs of the country?
options: The service, loyalty and hard work of its citizens
mcqs.why: The country's needs are honest work in every field, respect for laws, unity, and sacrifice for the nation's progress and defence.

mcqs.q: We must answer the country's needs under the name of ______.
mcqs.why: Citizenship is the position of being a citizen of a country: 'Under the name of citizenship, give your country her due.'

mcqs.q: In the model answer, the writer wants to serve Pakistan as a ______.
options: teacher, so that every child can read and write
mcqs.why: The model: study hard, obey laws, keep surroundings clean, help the poor, and serve Pakistan as a teacher when grown up.

mcqs.q: 'Deserve' means ______.
options: to do something or show some quality
to be worthy of something because of what one has done
mcqs.why: The solved content corrects the book glossary's misprint: in the poem, 'deserve' means to be worthy of — 'Such a country deserves some help from you.'

mcqs.q: 'Patriotic' means ______.
mcqs.why: Patriotic means expressing devotion for one's country: 'We should pay our debt with patriotic words and deeds.'

mcqs.q: 'Unafraid' means ______.
mcqs.why: Unafraid means feeling no fear or anxiety: 'The soldiers stood unafraid before the enemy.'

lessons.title: Activity and Vocabulary: Gist Writing, Transitive and Intransitive Verbs
lessons.notes_html:
Gist Writing — 'Human Competition'

The gist of a paragraph gives its main points. Gist of the paragraph: Human competition is a contest in which two or more people strive for a goal that cannot be shared, usually resulting in a victor and a loser, so individuals and groups must struggle to achieve the outcome. The writer believes competition acts as a motivational factor: it makes a person work hard to get effective results, and it is natural to give our best to survive. Competitions encourage students to give their best to achieve excellence; thus competition is not just necessary for the learning process, it is itself learning. The present world is the world of competition, where one has to win to prove one's capability. However, some believe competition is necessary for learning, while others believe it is not at all good and distracts from learning.

Transitive and Intransitive Verbs

A transitive verb denotes an action which passes over from the subject to an object; an intransitive verb denotes an action which does not pass over to an object.

  • Transitive: The fire burns the house. (object: the house) Tell the truth. The girl cut the vegetables. I locked the door.
  • Intransitive: The birds chirp in the morning. The kid sleeps on the bed. The old man asked for alms. (no direct object; 'for alms' is a prepositional phrase) The tiger lives in the jungle. The old woman sat down by the side of the road. The sun sets in the west.

mcqs.q: A gist of a paragraph gives ______.
mcqs.why: Gist writing sums up the main points — the gist exercise condenses the 'Human competition' paragraph into its central ideas.

mcqs.q: According to the gist, human competition is a contest in which ______.
options: two or more people strive for a goal that cannot be shared, usually resulting in a victor and a loser
mcqs.why: The gist begins with this definition of human competition, in which individuals and groups must struggle to achieve the outcome.

mcqs.q: The writer believes competition acts as ______.
options: a motivational factor that makes a person work hard to get effective results
mcqs.why: Competition motivates hard work and encourages students to give their best to achieve excellence; it is itself learning.

mcqs.q: According to the gist, some people believe competition ______.
options: is the only way to learn
is not at all good and distracts from learning
mcqs.why: The gist ends with the other view: some believe competition is necessary for learning, while others believe it distracts from learning.

mcqs.q: A transitive verb is one whose action ______.
options: is always in the past tense
passes over from the subject to an object
mcqs.why: The book defines: a transitive verb denotes an action which passes over to an object; an intransitive verb's action does not pass over to an object.

mcqs.q: In 'The fire burns the house', 'burns' is ______.
mcqs.why: The action passes to the object 'the house', so 'burns' is transitive here — like Tell (the truth), cut (the vegetables) and locked (the door).

mcqs.q: In 'The birds chirp in the morning', 'chirp' is ______.
mcqs.why: Chirp has no object; the action does not pass over to anything — intransitive, like sleeps, lives, sat and sets in the exercise.

mcqs.q: In 'The old man asked for alms', 'asked' is intransitive because ______.
options: 'for alms' is a prepositional phrase, not a direct object
mcqs.why: The solved answer notes that 'asked' has no direct object here; 'for alms' is only a prepositional phrase.

mcqs.q: Which verb is transitive in its sentence?
mcqs.why: Locked takes the object 'the door'. Sets, sleeps and lives in these sentences have no objects — they are intransitive.

mcqs.q: 'Tell the truth' — 'Tell' is transitive because ______.
options: it is in the present tense
mcqs.why: The action of telling passes over to the object 'the truth', making 'Tell' a transitive verb.

lessons.title: Grammar: Adjective Phrases and Clauses, Reported Questions, Semi-colon and Colon
lessons.notes_html:
Adjective Phrases

An adjective phrase acts like an adjective in a sentence and modifies a noun or pronoun.

  • 'covered in mud' — modifies 'Students'. 'very expansive' — modifies 'shoes'.
  • 'Slow and steady' — describes the subject (the one who wins the race).
  • 'of the English language' — modifies 'rules'. 'about her annual result' — modifies 'Sara'. 'of words' — modifies 'man'.

Adjective Clauses

An adjective clause is a group of words which contains a subject and a predicate of its own and does the work of an adjective.

  • 'who won the award' — modifies 'girl'. 'where he lives' — modifies 'building'.
  • 'which I like' — modifies 'story book'. 'who wants the textbook' — modifies 'Sana'. 'that Alia is driving' — modifies 'car'.
  • Note: In 'The boy sitting next to me is kind', there is NO adjective clause; 'sitting next to me' is an adjective (participial) phrase modifying 'boy', because it has no finite verb of its own.

Reported Questions

In reporting questions, the indirect speech is introduced by verbs like asked/inquired; when the question is not introduced by an interrogative word, the reporting verb is followed by 'whether' or 'if', and the question form changes into the statement form.

  • She asked if/whether she was late.
  • He asked if/whether they were in London.
  • Samina asked if/whether the bus stop was near the school.
  • Kamran asked if/whether my father took tea.
  • I asked him if/whether he could help me.
  • Daniyal asked if/whether he had arrived on time.
  • Madiha asked if/whether I would come later.
  • He asked if/whether I had been to Kashmir.

Semi-colon and Colon

A semi-colon is used between two separate statements linked in meaning, and to separate the clauses of compound sentences: 'Ali is a kind person; he always helps the poor.' 'It was raining heavily; however, we still went to school.' A colon is used before an explanation or a list, to introduce a single thing for emphasis: 'There are four seasons in Pakistan: summer, winter, spring and autumn.' 'He had only one aim in life: to serve his country.'

mcqs.q: An adjective phrase ______.
options: has its own subject and predicate
acts like an adjective and modifies a noun or pronoun
mcqs.why: An adjective phrase modifies a noun or pronoun — 'covered in mud' modifies Students; 'of words' modifies man.

mcqs.q: In 'Some rules of the English language are now null and void', the adjective phrase is ______.
mcqs.why: The solved answer identifies 'of the English language' as the adjective phrase modifying 'rules'.

mcqs.q: An adjective clause differs from an adjective phrase because it ______.
options: contains a subject and a predicate of its own
mcqs.why: An adjective clause does the work of an adjective but has its own subject and predicate — 'who won the award' modifies 'girl'.

mcqs.q: In 'The boy sitting next to me is kind', 'sitting next to me' is ______.
options: an adjective (participial) phrase, not a clause
mcqs.why: It has no finite verb of its own, so it is a participial phrase modifying 'boy' — the solved answer stresses there is no adjective clause in this sentence.

mcqs.q: She asked, 'Am I late?' → indirect: ______.
options: She asked that am I late
She asked if am I late
She asked if/whether she was late
She said if she is late
mcqs.why: Yes/no questions are reported with if/whether, and the question form changes into statement form: She asked if she was late.

mcqs.q: Daniyal said, 'Did he arrive on time?' → indirect: ______.
options: Daniyal asked did he arrive on time
Daniyal asked if he arrives on time
Daniyal said that he arrived on time yesterday
Daniyal asked if/whether he had arrived on time
mcqs.why: The past question becomes a statement with the past perfect: Daniyal asked whether he had arrived on time.

mcqs.q: In reported questions, when there is no interrogative word (who/what/where), we use ______ after the reporting verb.
mcqs.why: The book's rule: the reporting verb (asked/inquired) is followed by 'whether' or 'if' when the question is not introduced by an interrogative word.

mcqs.q: A semi-colon is used ______.
options: between two separate statements linked in meaning
at the end of a question
mcqs.why: Semi-colon examples: 'Ali is a kind person; he always helps the poor.' 'The sun has set; the stars have appeared.'

mcqs.q: A colon is used ______.
options: before an explanation or a list, or to introduce a single thing for emphasis
in place of a comma always
mcqs.why: Colon examples: 'There are four seasons in Pakistan: summer, winter, spring and autumn.' 'He had only one aim in life: to serve his country.'

mcqs.q: In 'The car that Alia is driving is of red colour', the adjective clause is ______.
mcqs.why: The clause 'that Alia is driving' has its own subject (Alia) and predicate (is driving) and modifies 'car' — an adjective clause.

lessons.title: Writing: Poem Summary, Magazine Article and Own Poem
lessons.notes_html:
Summary of the Poem 'Give to Your Country' (by Lenore Hetrick)

The poet says that our dear country is great and good. All the laws made in it are meant to keep us happy and well, peaceful and unafraid. Such a country, therefore, deserves some help from us: under the name of citizenship we must give our country her due. We should give her our service, give her our all and our best, and let our actions and words prove a wealth of love for her. We owe a debt to our country, and this debt is paid with patriotic words and deeds. Under the name of citizenship, we must answer our country's needs.

Magazine Article — 'My City Faisalabad' (Model)

'Faisalabad is my native city. It is one of the biggest cities of Punjab, Pakistan, and is famous as an industrial city, especially for its textile mills and cloth markets. The city was founded in 1892 and was first named Lyallpur. Its clock tower, built in the British period, stands in the centre of eight bazaars which are laid out in the design of the Union Jack flag. Faisalabad is also an agricultural city: the University of Agriculture here is famous all over the country, and the fertile land around it produces bumper crops of wheat, cotton and sugarcane. Facts to know: Province: Punjab. Famous for: textiles and cloth. Landmark: Clock Tower (Ghanta Ghar). University: University of Agriculture Faisalabad.'

Own Poem — 'For My Country' (Model)

'O my dear country, great and good, / I give you service, as I should. / Peaceful and unafraid we stand, / With love and pride for our homeland. / You keep us happy, safe and well, / Your gifts are more than words can tell. / Under the name of citizenship true, / I give my country her due. / With patriotic words and deeds, / I'll answer all my country's needs.'

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Give to Your Country'?
mcqs.why: The summary names the poem 'Give to Your Country' as by Lenore Hetrick — the same poet as 'The Earth Speaks'.

mcqs.q: According to the summary, such a country ______ some help from us.
mcqs.why: Because the country is great and good and its laws keep us happy and well, it deserves some help from us.

mcqs.q: Faisalabad was founded in ______ and was first named ______.
mcqs.why: The article states the city was founded in 1892 and was first named Lyallpur.

mcqs.q: The eight bazaars of Faisalabad are laid out in the design of ______.
mcqs.why: The clock tower stands in the centre of eight bazaars laid out in the design of the Union Jack flag, built in the British period.

mcqs.q: Faisalabad is famous for ______.
options: textiles and cloth (its textile mills and cloth markets)
mcqs.why: The article's facts box: Province — Punjab; Famous for — textiles and cloth; Landmark — Clock Tower (Ghanta Ghar); University — University of Agriculture Faisalabad.

mcqs.q: The landmark of Faisalabad is ______.
mcqs.why: The article names the Clock Tower (Ghanta Ghar), built in the British period, as the city's landmark.

mcqs.q: In the model poem, the poet promises: 'With patriotic words and deeds, ______.'
options: I'll answer all my country's needs
mcqs.why: The poem ends: 'With patriotic words and deeds, / I'll answer all my country's needs.'

mcqs.q: The model poem uses which words from the original poem?
options: 'great and good', 'peaceful and unafraid', 'citizenship', 'patriotic words and deeds'
mcqs.why: The writing task required using words from 'Give to Your Country' — the model uses great and good, peaceful and unafraid, citizenship and patriotic words and deeds.

mcqs.q: The summary says we must give our country ______.
options: her due, under the name of citizenship
mcqs.why: 'Under the name of citizenship we must give our country her due... give her our service, give her our all and our best.'

mcqs.q: The article calls the people of Faisalabad ______.
mcqs.why: The article ends: 'The people of my city are hardworking and hospitable, and I am proud of my native city.'

lessons.title: Reading: Trees Plantation
lessons.notes_html:
The Diary

The text is a diary written by a school student who signs it as 'BB — Your best buddy'. The diary entries of 21st March and 25th March 2022 describe the National Tree Plantation Day celebrations at his/her school.

National Tree Plantation Day

It is the day celebrated (here on 21st March, 2022) to plant trees and create awareness about their importance. At the writer's school, the teachers and the school gardener Uncle Riaz planted a plant of roses in the school garden, and the head teacher told the students why planting trees is necessary: the cutting of trees has increased the risk of natural disasters. If we want to save our earth and the creatures living on it, we should plant more and more trees to make the mother earth beautiful and green. Cutting trees also increases pollution and climate change, which the Government's 'Go Green' goal aims to confront.

How the Students Planted Saplings

On 25th March the students were divided into groups. Each group shovelled a small area and planted a sapling there; after that they watered it and prayed to Allah to make it grow healthy and strong. (Steps of sapling plantation: dig/shovel the soil, place the sapling, cover the roots with soil, and water it regularly.) The class teacher assigned duties and duty days on a chart in the class, so the students look after their saplings regularly. The group whose sapling grows into a healthy tree will be rewarded on the next year's plantation day.

Planting at Home

The writer asked his father to bring plant pots to their home as a surprise for Mom, to see a bright smile on her face — because whatever we learn from school benefits us at home.

Besides Planting Trees

We can keep our surroundings clean, avoid throwing litter in streets and rivers, save water and electricity, reduce the use of plastic bags, use public transport or bicycles to lessen smoke, and protect the plants and animals around us. We should also use recycled things — as Nasir did, making pots of different designs from used plastic bottles to plant seedlings at home.

Word Meanings

  • decrease — to become less in number or amount. disaster — a sudden event causing great damage or loss.
  • pollution — the presence of harmful substances in the environment. sapling — a young tree.
  • rewarded — given something in return for good work. promise — a statement that one will definitely do something.

mcqs.q: The writer of the diary signs it as ______.
mcqs.why: The diary is written by a school student who signs as 'BB — Your best buddy'; its entries of 21st and 25th March 2022 describe the Plantation Day at school.

mcqs.q: The National Tree Plantation Day at the writer's school was celebrated on ______.
mcqs.why: The diary entry of 21st March 2022 describes the celebration; on 25th March the students planted saplings in groups.

mcqs.q: Who planted a plant of roses in the school garden?
options: The teachers and the school gardener Uncle Riaz
mcqs.why: The teachers and the gardener Uncle Riaz planted a plant of roses, and the head teacher told the students why planting trees is necessary.

mcqs.q: Cutting of trees has increased the risk of ______.
mcqs.why: The head teacher told the students in the morning assembly that cutting trees has increased the risk of natural disasters; it also increases pollution and climate change.

mcqs.q: How did the students plant the saplings?
options: Each student planted alone without help
Each group shovelled a small area, planted a sapling, watered it and prayed for its growth
The gardener planted all the saplings
They placed saplings on the roof
mcqs.why: On 25th March the students were divided into groups; each group dug the soil, placed the sapling, covered the roots, watered it and prayed to Allah.

mcqs.q: Which group will be rewarded on the next Plantation Day?
options: The group that plants the most saplings
The group that comes first to school
The group whose sapling grows into a healthy tree
The group with the biggest plant pot
mcqs.why: The head teacher announced that the group whose sapling grows into a healthy tree will be rewarded the next year; looking after it is the group's duty.

mcqs.q: How will the students keep their plants healthy?
options: By asking the gardener to do everything
The class teacher assigned duties and duty days on a chart in the class
mcqs.why: A duty chart in the class shows everyone's duty and duty day, so the saplings are watered and cared for regularly.

mcqs.q: Why did the writer ask his father to bring plants home?
options: As a surprise for Mom, to see a bright smile on her face
To sell them in the market
mcqs.why: Whatever we learn from school benefits us at home — he wanted to surprise his mother with plant pots and see her smile.

mcqs.q: Besides planting trees, we can make the earth healthy by ______.
options: saving water and electricity and reducing the use of plastic bags
mcqs.why: Other steps: keep surroundings clean, avoid littering streets and rivers, save water and electricity, use public transport or bicycles, and use recycled things — like Nasir's pots from used plastic bottles.

mcqs.q: A 'sapling' is ______.
mcqs.why: The dictionary meanings define a sapling as a young tree: 'Each group planted a sapling in the school ground.'

lessons.title: Grammar: Sentence Types and Reported Speech — Requests, Commands and Exclamations
lessons.notes_html:
Simple, Compound and Complex Sentences

A simple sentence has one subject and one predicate. A compound sentence connects two or more independent clauses by a co-ordinating conjunction or semicolon. A complex sentence consists of one main clause and one or more subordinate clauses.

  • 'The gardener waters the plants.' — Simple.
  • 'This is the building that Mustafa designed.' — Complex (main clause + subordinate adjective clause 'that Mustafa designed').
  • 'A hundred paisa makes a rupee.' — Simple.
  • 'The chair on which he sat costs five thousand rupees.' — Complex (main clause + subordinate clause 'on which he sat').
  • 'These sums are too difficult for me to solve.' — Simple.

Reporting Requests and Commands

In reporting commands and requests, the indirect speech is introduced by a verb expressing command or request — ordered, requested, advised, told — followed by 'to' + verb; the negative command takes 'not to'.

  • He ordered/told his younger brother to finish his homework.
  • He requested his friends to have a lunch with his family the next day at 2 o'clock.
  • The doctor advised the patient to take medicines on time.
  • The teacher advised/ordered the students not to waste their time in talking.
  • Fahad requested his boss to increase his salary.
  • The police ordered (the men) to catch the robbers.

Exclamatory Sentences in Reported Speech

An exclamatory sentence expresses joy, sorrow or wonder; in indirect speech we add words like 'exclaimed with joy', 'exclaimed with sorrow' or 'exclaimed with wonder'.

  • The child exclaimed with wonder that it was a very beautiful sight.
  • The lady exclaimed with wonder that the girl was very beautiful.
  • The student wished the teacher good morning respectfully.
  • The boy exclaimed with joy that he had won a prize.
  • The emperor exclaimed with sorrow that their foes were too strong.
  • She exclaimed with sorrow that she was undone. / that they had lost the match (pity).
  • They exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
  • The father prayed that his son might live long.

mcqs.q: 'The gardener waters the plants' is a ______ sentence.
mcqs.why: It has one subject and one predicate — a simple sentence, like 'A hundred paisa makes a rupee.'

mcqs.q: 'This is the building that Mustafa designed' is a ______ sentence.
mcqs.why: It has a main clause ('This is the building') plus a subordinate adjective clause ('that Mustafa designed') — a complex sentence.

mcqs.q: A compound sentence ______.
options: has one subject and one predicate
has a main clause and a subordinate clause
connects two or more independent clauses by a co-ordinating conjunction or semicolon
mcqs.why: The book defines the three kinds: simple (one subject, one predicate), compound (independent clauses joined), complex (main + subordinate clauses).

mcqs.q: He said to his younger brother, 'Finish your homework.' → indirect: ______.
options: He said his brother to finish homework
He ordered his brother that finish his homework
He told his brother finished his homework
He ordered/told his younger brother to finish his homework
mcqs.why: Commands are reported with a verb of command (ordered/told) + 'to' + verb.

mcqs.q: The teacher said to the students, 'Do not waste your time in talking.' → indirect: ______.
options: The teacher advised/ordered the students not to waste their time in talking
The teacher told the students to not waste time in talking yesterday
The teacher said students do not waste time
The teacher ordered students waste their time
mcqs.why: A negative command takes 'not to': the teacher advised the students not to waste their time in talking.

mcqs.q: The doctor said to the patient, 'Take medicines on time.' → the reporting verb is ______.
mcqs.why: The solved answer uses 'advised' for a doctor: 'The doctor advised the patient to take medicines on time.' Police use 'ordered' and Fahad 'requested' his boss.

mcqs.q: The child said, 'What a beautiful sight!' → reported: ______.
options: The child said that what a beautiful sight
The child exclaimed with joy that it is a beautiful sight
The child exclaimed with wonder that it was a very beautiful sight
The child asked what a beautiful sight it was
mcqs.why: Exclamations of wonder are reported with 'exclaimed with wonder', and 'is' changes to 'was' with 'very' replacing 'what a'.

mcqs.q: The boy cried, 'Hurrah! I won a prize.' → reported: ______.
options: The boy exclaimed with sorrow that he won a prize
The boy said hurrah he won a prize
The boy exclaimed with wonder that he has won a prize
The boy exclaimed with joy that he had won a prize
mcqs.why: 'Hurrah!' shows joy: exclaimed with joy, and 'won' (simple past) becomes 'had won' (past perfect).

mcqs.q: The emperor said, 'Alas! Our foes are too strong.' → reported with ______.
mcqs.why: 'Alas!' expresses sorrow: 'The emperor exclaimed with sorrow that their foes were too strong.' 'May you live long!' is reported as a prayer.

mcqs.q: Fahad said to his boss, 'Please increase my salary.' → indirect: ______.
options: Fahad ordered his boss to increase his salary
Fahad requested his boss to increase his salary
Fahad said his boss to increase salary
Fahad requested his boss that increase his salary
mcqs.why: 'Please' shows a request, so the reporting verb is 'requested' followed by 'to' + verb.

lessons.title: Writing: Diary Page, Email and Formal Letter
lessons.notes_html:
Diary Page — A School Trip to a Park (Model)

'Date: 15th April, 2022. Dear Diary, Today we went on a school trip to the park with our class teacher, and it was really a fun day. We reached the park at nine o'clock. First we walked among the green trees and colourful flowers, and our teacher told us the names of many plants. Then we played on the swings and slides, and ate the lunch we had brought from home under a big shady tree. Before leaving, we cleaned the place and threw all the litter in the dustbins, because we must keep our parks clean. I also planted a small sapling near the gate with my friends. I will come back to you when I visit the park again. See you soon, my dear friend. Your best buddy, BB.'

Email to a Friend (Model)

Format: To, Subject, Greetings, Body, Closing. 'To: abcpakistan@gmail.com. Subject: Let Us Plant Saplings to Make the Earth Green. Dear Fahad, I hope you and your family are in the best of health. Last week we celebrated the National Tree Plantation Day at our school. Our head teacher told us that the cutting of trees has increased the risk of natural disasters, and if we want to save our earth and the creatures living on it, we should plant more and more trees. I planted a sapling with my group, and we have promised to look after it. I encourage you to plant saplings at your school and at home too — you can even make pots from old plastic bottles, as my friend Nasir did. Together we can make our earth beautiful and green... Your loving friend, Asjad Javed.'

Formal Letter — Parts and Difference from Informal Letters

Parts of the formal letter (to the Director of Education about the shortage of textbooks): (1) Sender's address — 321-Omar Block, Allama Iqbal Town, Lahore. (2) Date — April 21, 2022. (3) Receiver's address/designation — The Managing Director, Punjab Curriculum & Textbook Board, Lahore. (4) Salutation — Respected Sir. (5) Subject — 'Paucity of Textbooks in the Area of Allama Iqbal Town, Lahore.' (6) Body — the writer draws attention to the paucity of textbooks; the students of Grade VIII are facing problems and suffering great loss in their studies; requests that the availability of textbooks be ensured at the earliest. (7) Closing — 'Hope for a favourable response.' (8) Subscription and signature — Yours sincerely, Farhana Zulfiqar.

Difference: A formal letter is written to an official or a stranger for business/official purposes; it has a subject line, a respectful salutation (Respected Sir/Madam), formal and to-the-point language, and closes with 'Yours sincerely/faithfully'. An informal letter is written to friends and relatives; it has no subject line, uses a friendly greeting (Dear Friend), personal and free language, and closes with 'Your friend' or 'Your loving friend'.

mcqs.q: The model diary page is dated ______.
mcqs.why: The diary model begins 'Date: 15th April, 2022' and narrates the school trip to the park; it is signed 'Your best buddy, BB'.

mcqs.q: On the park trip, before leaving, the students ______.
options: cleaned the place and threw all the litter in the dustbins
mcqs.why: The diary says they cleaned the place and threw litter in the dustbins, because we must keep our parks clean.

mcqs.q: An email is written in the format ______.
mcqs.why: The book's email format is: To, Subject, Greetings, Body, Closing — as in the model email to Fahad.

mcqs.q: The subject of the model email is ______.
options: 'Let Us Plant Saplings to Make the Earth Green'
mcqs.why: The email to abcpakistan@gmail.com carries the subject 'Let Us Plant Saplings to Make the Earth Green' and is signed by Asjad Javed.

mcqs.q: In the email, the writer encourages his friend to ______.
options: buy plants from a nursery only
plant saplings at school and at home, even making pots from old plastic bottles like Nasir
mcqs.why: He writes: 'you can even make pots from old plastic bottles, as my friend Nasir did. Together we can make our earth beautiful and green.'

mcqs.q: The formal letter is written about ______.
options: the paucity (shortage) of textbooks in Allama Iqbal Town, Lahore
mcqs.why: Its subject line reads: 'Paucity of Textbooks in the Area of Allama Iqbal Town, Lahore' — the students of Grade VIII are suffering great loss in their studies.

mcqs.q: The formal letter is addressed to ______.
options: The Managing Director, Punjab Curriculum & Textbook Board, Lahore
mcqs.why: The receiver's designation given in the parts is The Managing Director, Punjab Curriculum & Textbook Board, Lahore; the salutation is 'Respected Sir'.

mcqs.q: A formal letter differs from an informal letter because it ______.
options: has a subject line, a respectful salutation and formal, to-the-point language
mcqs.why: Formal letters close with 'Yours sincerely/faithfully'; informal letters have no subject line, use friendly greetings and close with 'Your loving friend'.

mcqs.q: The formal letter closes (subscription) with ______.
mcqs.why: The subscription and signature of the formal letter are 'Yours sincerely, Farhana Zulfiqar'; the sender's address is 321-Omar Block, Allama Iqbal Town, Lahore.

mcqs.q: In the diary model, the class reached the park at ______.
mcqs.why: The diary says: 'We reached the park at nine o'clock. First we walked among the green trees and colourful flowers...'
